policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the participle: 'a man called by name Zacchaeus'. The omission leaves nothing for 'called'.
ASV 'and he was a chief publican' renders either the pronoun or the demonstrative with copula; ASV regularly renders houtos as 'he' in narrative resumption.
Both readings yield the same purpose clause; ASV 'to see him' does not distinguish the articular infinitive from the conjunction with subjunctive.
ASV has only 'he looked up, and said unto him'; the added 'saw him and' is unrepresented.
Orthographic/declensional variants of 'half'; ASV 'the half of my goods' renders either.
Word order only; ASV 'of my goods' is identical under either arrangement.
Word order only; ASV 'I give to the poor' follows English order regardless.
Word order only; ASV 'because he was nigh to Jerusalem' does not preserve Greek sequence here.
ASV 'Trade ye herewith' is a second person plural imperative, not the infinitive.
ASV 'till I come' renders either the temporal relative phrase or the conjunction; the former is commonly rendered 'until/while I come'.
ASV 'unto whom he had given the money' renders the pluperfect; the aorist would give 'gave'.
ASV 'that he might know what they had gained' has no interrogative 'who'; the added tis is unrepresented.
ASV 'what they had gained by trading' is plural, matching the third plural verb, not the singular.
Word order and spelling of the augment only; ASV 'hath made ten pounds more' renders either.
ASV 'Well done' renders the adverb with or without the enclitic particle.
ASV 'Thy pound, Lord, hath made' places the vocative after the subject, excluding the RP order that fronts 'Lord'; the remaining two differ only in punctuation of the vocative.
Word order only; ASV 'Be thou also over five cities' renders either.
The ASV note glosses the Greek as 'the other', with the definite article of the base reading; the anarthrous reading would be simply 'another'.
ASV 'He saith unto him' opens without a conjunction; the ASV renders postpositive de regularly, so the added particle is unrepresented.
Word order only; ASV 'my money' renders either.
Word order only; ASV 'should have required it' renders either.
ASV 'I say unto you, that unto every one that hath' has no 'for'; the added particle is unrepresented.
ASV 'shall be taken away from him' renders the added prepositional phrase, which the base reading lacks.
ASV 'But these mine enemies' renders the near demonstrative, not 'those'.
ASV 'and slay them before me' has an unitalicized object pronoun, which the omitting reading does not supply.
ASV 'two of the disciples', not 'his disciples'; the added possessive is unrepresented.
Both participles of 'say' yield ASV 'saying'.
ASV 'loose him, and bring him' turns the participle into a coordinated imperative, so its 'and' is required whether or not the Greek conjunction stands.
ASV 'thus shall ye say' has no indirect object; the added pronoun is unrepresented.
Recitative hoti is left untranslated before direct speech, so ASV 'And they said, The Lord hath need of him' does not distinguish it from the omission.
ASV 'their garments' renders either the personal or the reflexive genitive plural.
ASV 'their garments' renders either the reflexive or the personal genitive plural.
Gender agreement only; ASV 'for all the mighty works' renders either.
ASV 'Blessed is the King that cometh' takes its definite article from the articular participle, so the second article is not distinguished.
Word order only; ASV 'peace in heaven' follows English order regardless.
ASV 'And he answered and said, I tell you' has no 'unto them'; the added pronoun is unrepresented.
ASV 'I tell you that, if these shall hold their peace' renders the conjunction 'that', which the omitting reading lacks.
Future indicative versus aorist subjunctive after ean; ASV 'if these shall hold their peace' renders either.
Both are future forms of the same verb; ASV 'will cry out' renders either.
Case of the object of epi only; ASV 'wept over it' renders either.

ASV 'in this day, even thou' keeps the temporal phrase before the pronoun and reads 'this day' rather than 'thy day'; the ASV note 'Some ancient authorities read this thy day' shows the possessive was not in the text rendered.
ASV text reads 'the things which belong unto peace' and relegates the possessive to the note 'Some ancient authorities read thy peace', so the added pronoun is the margin, not the text.
ASV 'shall cast up a bank about thee', with the note 'Greek palisade' glossing the noun, does not distinguish the verbal prefix.
Word order and case of the second 'stone' only; ASV 'leave in thee one stone upon another' renders either.
ASV 'cast out them that sold' stops there; 'in it and them that bought' is unrepresented.
ASV 'And my house shall be a house of prayer' renders both the conjunction and the future copula that the omitting reading lacks.
ASV's future 'shall be' rests on the earlier future copula; the added present 'is' would give 'my house is a house of prayer'.
Augment spelling only; ASV 'they could not find' renders either.
